definition: The division label used for the Sanskrit epic’s eighteen books and for the declared Adi and Vana textual witnesses.
cultural_caution: A source-native textual-organization term, not a rigid chapter system across all recensions, translations, oral performances, or adaptations, and not a game campaign level.

supports: The Sanskrit text presents itself in eighteen books (parvans)

work_or_witness: Mahābhārata — Sanskrit epic-tradition orientation · Kanad Sinha, From Dāśarājña to Kurukṣetra, abstract
definition: A Sanskrit category discussed in scholarship on the Mahābhārata’s historical-tradition framing.
cultural_caution: Itihāsa must not be equated without qualification to modern academic history, colonial categories of ‘myth versus history,’ or a claim that the epic directly records verifiable events. Interpretations vary.

citations.locator: Kanad Sinha, From Dāśarājña to Kurukṣetra, abstract
supports: The scholarship discusses the Mahābhārata in relation to itihāsa/historical tradition while explicitly not claiming it is an authentic modern history

work_or_witness: Mahābhārata — Sanskrit epic-tradition orientation · Pamela Lothspeich, ‘Mahābhārata in Hindu Tradition,’ Introduction, lines 2603–2608
canonical_term: textual, oral, and performative Mahābhārata traditions
definition: The scholarly framework used here to mark the Mahābhārata as a plurality of traditions rather than a single exhaustive canon.
cultural_caution: This is a scholarly orientation label, not a license to collapse living regional, vernacular, devotional, commentarial, or performance traditions into a Sanskrit text or to rank them under a critical edition. It also does not settle colonial philological debates.

citations.locator: Pamela Lothspeich, ‘Mahābhārata in Hindu Tradition,’ Introduction, lines 2603–2608
supports: The work is best understood as narrative tradition because there are oral, textual, and performative versions
